text:
[compiler] Don't treat comparing a ref-reading function as a ref access (#37688)

## Summary

Fixes a false positive in the `react-hooks/refs` validation
(`ValidateNoRefAccessInRender`). Fixes #37521.

Comparing a function with `===` / `!==` was reported as "Cannot access
refs during render" whenever that function reads a ref when called, for
example a `useCallback` that closes over `ref.current`:

```js
const sampleFunc = useCallback(() => {
  ref.current = /* ... */;
}, []);
return sampleFunc !== other ? 'different' : 'same';
```

A binary operator never invokes its operands, so comparing function
identity cannot read `.current`. The `BinaryExpression` case validated
its operands with `validateNoRefValueAccess`, which treats a `Structure`
type carrying `fn.readRefEffect` the same as an actual ref value. This
switches it to `validateNoDirectRefValueAccess`, which only flags a
direct `RefValue` operand, so `ref.current === x` still errors while `fn
!== otherFn` no longer does.

## How did you test this change?

- Added the regression fixture
`allow-comparing-ref-accessing-function-identity` (input + `.expect.md`)
reproducing the pattern from the issue; it now compiles without error
and the eval result is `"different"`.
- Direct `ref.current` comparisons continue to error (existing fixtures
unchanged).
- Ran the full compiler snapshot suite with `yarn snap`: 1828 tests, no
regressions.
- Ported the same change to the Rust compiler
(`validate_no_ref_access_in_render.rs`): `yarn snap --rust` passes all
1828 fixtures against the Rust backend, and `scripts/test-rust-port.sh
ValidateNoRefAccessInRender` reports no TS/Rust divergence.

text:
### Motivation / Background This Pull Request has been created because `cache_version` checks a connection out of the pool on every call when the adapter returns `updated_at` as a string, which is what SQLite3 does. It needs the connection only to read its `default_timezone`, and the code says so itself: ```ruby # FIXME: checking out a connection for this is wasteful # we should store/cache this information in the schema cache # or similar. self.class.with_connection(&:default_timezone) == :utc && ``` `cache_key` calls `cache_version` as well, to know whether there is one, so a `cache_key_with_version`, and a cache `read`, `write` or `fetch` keyed by a record, do it twice. `read_multi`, which is what `render collection:, cached: true` uses, does it four times per record. In a profile of `read_multi` for 100 records that are all in a `MemoryStore`, 67% of the time is in `cache_version`, 52% inside `with_connection`, and 7% in reading the cache. It is not only time. With every connection of the pool in use by other threads, computing the cache version of a record that is already loaded waits for `checkout_timeout` and raises `ActiveRecord::ConnectionTimeoutError`. ### Detail This Pull Request changes `can_use_fast_cache_version?` to ask the type of the attribute instead of a connection. The adapter builds its time types with the `default_timezone` of the database (`extended_type_map`), and `Type::Internal::Timezone#is_utc?` falls back to `ActiveRecord.default_timezone` when the database sets none, which is what `AbstractAdapter#default_timezone` returns. That type is also what the slow path uses to cast the string to a time, so both paths now read the string in the same timezone by construction. - The type comes from the attribute of the record, and is unwrapped when it is a `TimeZoneConverter`, which is the case in an application (time zone aware attributes). - When the attribute has no time type of Active Record, for example `select("MAX(created_at) AS updated_at")` on a model without that column, a connection is asked as before. I measured the other shape too, keeping the value on the pool as the FIXME suggests. Finding the pool for the current role and shard is by itself about a third of a `cache_version` call when the thread already holds a connection, and the type needs no lookup at all. The version strings are the same as before, and so is the path taken, as long as the types of the model were loaded from a database with the same `default_timezone` as the current connection. No public interface changes, so there is no CHANGELOG entry. What it doesn't do: - PostgreSQL, MySQL2 and Trilogy return a `Time` before type cast, so they never reached this check and nothing changes for them. - `cache_key` still calls `cache_version` only to know whether there is one. #53333 is open for that. ### Additional information **Benchmark.** Measured on our machine (Docker, 4 CPUs of a Ryzen 9 7940HX laptop, Ruby 3.4.11 +YJIT, SQLite3 in memory), `main` at 6ed67f82 and this branch alternated, median of three runs. The script is in the commit message. | | main | this branch | | |---|---|---|---| | `cache_version` | 605.7k i/s | 3.121M i/s | 5.2× | | `cache_key_with_version` | 274.8k i/s | 1.109M i/s | 4.0× | | `read_multi`, 100 records, all hits | 1.052k i/s | 2.271k i/s | 2.2× | When the thread already holds a connection (`LEASED=1` in the script, one run), there is no check out to save, only the lookups: | | main | this branch | | |---|---|---|---| | `cache_version` | 1.146M i/s | 3.268M i/s | 2.9× | | `cache_key_with_version` | 491.1k i/s | 1.105M i/s | 2.3× | | `read_multi`, 100 records, all hits | 1.525k i/s | 2.288k i/s | 1.5× | A whole request that renders 100 cached partials, in process through the middleware stack, same machine, three alternated runs: 308 to 385 requests per second on `main` (median 349), 482 to 509 on this branch (median 483). The runs on `main` are noisy, so read it as the direction, not as a ratio.
Script for the whole request ```ruby # frozen_string_literal: true # RAILS_PATH= ruby --yjit cached_page_ips.rb require "bundler/inline" gemfile do source "https://rubygems.org" gem "rails", path: ENV.fetch("RAILS_PATH", ".") gem "sqlite3" gem "benchmark-ips" end ENV["RAILS_ENV"] = "production" ENV["DATABASE_URL"] = "sqlite3:#{File.join(Dir.tmpdir, "cached_page_ips.sqlite3")}" require "rails" require "active_record/railtie" require "action_controller/railtie" require "action_view/railtie" require "action_view/testing/resolvers" class BenchApp < Rails::Application config.load_defaults Rails::VERSION::STRING.to_f config.root = Dir.tmpdir config.eager_load = true config.enable_reloading = false config.secret_key_base = "secret" * 11 config.logger = Logger.new(File::NULL) config.cache_store = :memory_store config.action_controller.perform_caching = true end Rails.application.initialize! Rails.application.routes.draw { resources :posts, only: :index } ActiveRecord::Schema.verbose = false ActiveRecord::Schema.define do create_table :posts, force: true do |t| t.string :title t.timestamps end end class Post < ActiveRecord::Base; end class PostsController < ActionController::Base prepend_view_path ActionView::FixtureResolver.new( "posts/index.html.erb" => %(
    <%= render partial: "posts/post", collection: @posts, cached: true %>
), "posts/_post.html.erb" => %(
  • <%= post.title %>
    • \n) ) def index @posts = Post.order(:id).limit(100) end end now = Time.now.utc Post.insert_all(100.times.map { |i| { title: "Post #{i}", created_at: now, updated_at: now + i } }) get = -> do status, _, body = Rails.application.call(Rack::MockRequest.env_for("http://localhost/posts")) raise "status #{status}" unless status == 200 body.each { } body.close if body.respond_to?(:close) end get.call # fills the cache Benchmark.ips do |x| x.report("GET /posts, 100 cached partials", &get) end ```
    **Pool in use.** A pool of one connection, held by another thread, `checkout_timeout: 2`. On `main` `cache_version` returns after 2.000 s with `ActiveRecord::ConnectionTimeoutError`; on this branch it returns the version at once.
    Script for the pool in use ```ruby # frozen_string_literal: true # cd && bundle exec ruby pool_in_use.rb require "bundler/setup" require "active_record" require "tmpdir" db = File.join(Dir.tmpdir, "pool_in_use.sqlite3") File.delete(db) if File.exist?(db) ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(adapter: "sqlite3", database: db, pool: 1, checkout_timeout: 2) ActiveRecord::Schema.verbose = false ActiveRecord::Schema.define { create_table(:posts, force: true) { |t| t.timestamps } } ActiveRecord::Base.cache_versioning = true class Post < ActiveRecord::Base; end Post.create! post = Post.first ActiveRecord::Base.release_connection holding = Queue.new done = Queue.new other = Thread.new do ActiveRecord::Base.with_connection do holding << true done.pop end end holding.pop t = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) result = begin post.cache_version rescue => e "#{e.class}: #{e.message[0, 90]}" end elapsed = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t puts format("cache_version with the only connection in use elsewhere: %.3f s -> %s", elapsed, result) done << true other.join ```
    **Tests.** Six tests in `cache_key_test.rb`. Three assert that no connection is checked out (a record from the database, with time zone aware attributes, and with `updated_at` as an alias); on `main` they fail with `Expected with_connection to be called 0 times, but was called 1 times`. Three pin what must not change and pass on `main` too: the slow path when `ActiveRecord.default_timezone` is `:local`, the slow path when only the database configuration says `default_timezone: "local"`, and a computed `updated_at` column. Each new line was seen failing a test with that line changed (7 single changes, each caught). Run locally: the Active Record suites for SQLite3 (9,898 runs) and PostgreSQL (10,806 runs), no failures; the same suites on `main` have none either. MySQL2 and Trilogy were not run locally. ### Checklist Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked: * [x] This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs. * [x] Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this PR fixes a related issue include it in the commit message. ## Summary

Codegen emits `debugger;` without a source location, so Babel's source map attributes it to the end of the preceding statement. A debugger that pauses on it then shows the line above as the paused line, and one step over appears to skip the `debugger;` line. Coverage instrumentation also loses the statement.

Here, codegen gives the `Debugger` instruction's location to the `DebuggerStatement` through `withLoc`, as it does for other statements. The Rust compiler already does this. The source location validator now also tracks `DebuggerStatement`, as istanbul-lib-instrument does, in both compilers.

snap skipped `debugger` and `debugger-memoized` for the TS compiler because of "cosmetic blank-line differences" from the Rust output. Those differences came from the missing location: snap generates with `retainLines`, which uses `loc` to place statements. With this change the TS output matches the existing snapshots, so the fixtures are no longer skipped.

## How did you test this change?

- New fixture `debugger-source-locations` (`@validateSourceLocations`). Without the codegen change it fails with "Source location for DebuggerStatement is missing in the generated output". With the change it passes. Under `yarn snap --rust` it fails if the location is removed from the Rust codegen.

text:
## Summary
Minor performance optimizations in `requests/auth.py`, specifically in
`HTTPDigestAuth`. No behavioral or API changes — outputs are byte-for-byte
identical to before for all inputs.

## Changes

1. **Hoist digest hash-function closures to module scope**
   `build_digest_header()` previously defined four nested closures
   (`md5_utf8`, `sha_utf8`, `sha256_utf8`, `sha512_utf8`) on *every* call,
   i.e. on every digest-authenticated request. These are now module-level
   functions (`_md5_utf8`, etc.) selected once via a precomputed
   `_DIGEST_HASH_FUNCS` dict, replacing the if/elif chain with a single
   dict lookup.

2. **Compile the digest-scheme regex once**
   `handle_401()` recompiled `re.compile(r"digest ", flags=re.IGNORECASE)`
   on every 401 response. It's now a module-level constant
   (`_DIGEST_SCHEME_RE`) compiled once at import time.

3. **Single `bytes.join()` instead of repeated `+=`**
   The cnonce seed in `build_digest_header()` was built via four
   successive `+=` concatenations on a `bytes` object, each allocating a
   new object. Replaced with a single `b"".join(...)`.

## Why this is safe
- All three changes are pure refactors of *how* the same values are
  computed, not *what* is computed. Function bodies, algorithm selection
  logic, and string/byte outputs are unchanged.
- Existing test suite passes unmodified.

## Testing
- Ran the full `auth` test suite (`pytest tests/test_requests.py -k auth`) — all passing.
- Isolated microbenchmark (`timeit`, N=200,000) comparing old vs new
  implementations of the changed code paths:

  | Change                                   | Old (us/call) | New (us/call) | Speedup |
  |-------------------------------------------|---------------|----------------|---------|
  | Hash-function selection (closures → dict) | 0.167         | 0.071          | 2.3x    |
  | Regex stripping (compile → precompiled)   | 0.824         | 0.393          | 2.1x    |
  | cnonce seed (chained += → join)           | 2.180         | 1.952          | 1.1x    |

  These are microbenchmarks on the isolated logic, not end-to-end request
  timings — real-world impact is dominated by network I/O, but this removes
  unnecessary per-call allocation/compilation overhead on the digest-auth
  hot path, which matters under high request volume.

text:
This replaces `hydratable` with `Warp`, a `Map` whose contents get sent from the server to the client. It's built on devalue's new `unevalStream`, which sets up streaming SSR in the next PR in this stack. On its own, this PR shouldn't change behavior much: the server still waits for every promise before responding, just like `hydratable` does today.

```js
import { Warp } from 'svelte';

const warp = new Warp('my-lib');
const user = await warp.getOrInsertComputed('user', () => getUser());
```

Each `Warp` has an id, so libraries don't collide with each other. `hydratable` is now just an internal `Warp`, and is deprecated. It's deprecated in JSDoc only, with no runtime warning: a warn-once-per-process message would make tests pass or fail depending on the order they run in. On the client, `Warp` behaves like a real `Map` (`set`, `delete` and friends all work), so it doubles as a cache. On the server, each key can only be set once, and `delete` and `clear` throw. Something may already have read the value during the render, or it may already be on its way to the client, so replacing it would mean the client hydrates with different data than the server rendered with. `getOrInsert(Computed)` is unaffected, and uses the native `Map` method when there is one.

There's also `withWarp` in `svelte/server`, for adding values before a render starts (in load functions, for example). A `render` inside it uses its context, and only one `render` is allowed per `withWarp`. Both `withWarp` and `render` take a devalue `replacer`. When both are given, the render's replacer runs first.

How the serialization works: the whole store goes through a single `unevalStream` call, and we read the tail to the end immediately and append it to the head script. Promises that have already settled are resolved in that same `<script>` before hydration runs, so the output is still a single `<script>`, as before, and devalue handles nested promises itself.

- Rejected promises now reject on the client, after passing through `render`'s `transformError`, and the client's `failed` boundary can handle them. Previously a rejection failed the whole render.
- Values that can't be serialized still fail the render, with `warp_serialization_failed`. If the problem is in the head, `unevalStream` throws. If it's in a resolved value, devalue passes a `DevalueError` to `transformError`, which we catch and rethrow once the tail is done. The error includes devalue's path to the bad value.
- `unresolved_hydratable` is now `unresolved_warp`, and is less precise. It fires if the tail isn't done within a macrotask of the render finishing, but it can't say which key is responsible, because devalue doesn't know. Since `unresolved_warp` is basically temporary, that seemed fine.

Tests: `warp.test.ts` covers the server API, `withWarp`, replacers, rejections and escaping. The runtime samples from the old `elliott/warp` branch are ported, plus a new `warp-rejected` sample where a server rejection ends up in a client `failed` snippet.

One thing to sort out before merging: devalue's `types.d.ts` uses `AsyncIterableIterator<string, void>`, which needs TS 5.6, so `pnpm check` fails on our 5.5.4 unless you pass `--skipLibCheck`. This should probably be fixed in devalue rather than here. It's on the prerelease build anyway, until devalue ships `unevalStream`.

text:
### Motivation / Background

Follow-up to #58834 and #58855.

A relocatable extension (`btree_gin`, `pg_trgm`, `hstore`, ...) can live in a schema that `dump_schemas` does not cover. The Ruby schema dump then writes the schema-qualified `enable_extension`, but no `create_schema`:

```ruby
ActiveRecord::Schema[8.2].define(version: 0) do
  enable_extension "extensions.btree_gin"
  enable_extension "plpgsql"
end
```

`db:schema:load` on a new database fails:

```
ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid: PG::InvalidSchemaName: ERROR:  schema "extensions" does not exist
```

#58855 fixed this for extensions whose control file fixes the schema (`postgis_tiger_geocoder`). Relocatable extensions keep their schema prefix, so they still fail on `main` (checked on 0aeb65829). We hit this while upgrading an app to Rails 8.1: its event-sourcing library installs `btree_gin` and `pg_trgm` in its own schema, and `dump_schemas` is `"public"`.

Reproduction (single file, needs a local PostgreSQL):

<details>
<summary>repro.rb</summary>

```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"

  gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main"
  gem "pg"
end

require "active_record"
require "minitest/autorun"
require "logger"
require "tempfile"

ENV["DATABASE_URL"] ||= "postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres"
DB_NAME = "schema_dump_extension_repro"

ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(ENV["DATABASE_URL"])
ActiveRecord::Base.connection.drop_database(DB_NAME)
ActiveRecord::Base.connection.create_database(DB_NAME)
ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection("#{ENV["DATABASE_URL"].sub(%r{/[^/]*\z}, "")}/#{DB_NAME}")
ActiveRecord::Base.logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :posts
  create_schema "extensions"
  enable_extension "extensions.btree_gin" # relocatable: its control file sets no schema
end

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_dumped_schema_loads_into_an_empty_database
    ActiveRecord.dump_schemas = "public"

    schema = Tempfile.new(["schema", ".rb"])
    ActiveRecord::SchemaDumper.dump(ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool, schema)
    schema.close

    connection = ActiveRecord::Base.connection
    connection.drop_table :posts
    connection.disable_extension "extensions.btree_gin"
    connection.drop_schema "extensions"

    load schema.path # PG::InvalidSchemaName: schema "extensions" does not exist
    assert connection.extension_enabled?("btree_gin")
  end
end
```

</details>

### Detail

This Pull Request changes `PostgreSQL::SchemaDumper#schemas` to also dump the schemas that dumped extensions are qualified with, when `dump_schemas` leaves them out:

```ruby
create_schema "extensions", if_not_exists: true
enable_extension "extensions.btree_gin"
```

- `if_not_exists: true` keeps the dump loadable where the platform creates the schema already (Supabase's `extensions` or `graphql`). That was the reason #58834 ruled out a plain `create_schema`.
- Schemas in `dump_schemas` keep the plain `create_schema`, so existing dumps do not change.
- `public` and `pg_*` schemas are skipped: they always exist, and PostgreSQL rejects `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS pg_catalog` ("The prefix "pg_" is reserved for system schemas").
- The dumper reads `connection.extensions` once and uses it for both `schemas` and `extensions`.

### Additional information

The reproduction above passes against this branch. `test/cases/adapters/postgresql/**/*_test.rb` and `test/cases/schema_dumper_test.rb` pass locally on PostgreSQL 14 (995 runs, 0 failures). The new `extension_schema_dump_test.rb` fails without the change.

The other option is to skip `enable_extension` for extensions in schemas outside `dump_schemas`, as for tables and enum types. I did not take it, because the loaded database would then miss extensions the app needs.

#18944 fixed #18941 by changing the condition under which the state proxy's `has` trap creates a source for a key, from `active_effect !== null` to `active_reaction !== null`. That makes `in` and `Object.hasOwn` reactive in a derived with no parent effect. It also stops creating the source whenever an effect is active but no reaction is (`active_effect !== null && active_reaction === null`). For example:

- while a component initialises
- in an `$effect.root` callback
- in an effect teardown that runs while an effect is active, such as when the effect re-runs
- after a top-level `await` in a component's script

The source isn't only used for tracking. It holds the key's current value, or marks a missing key as missing. Without it, a later write inside a fork creates the source in the `set` trap starting from `undefined`. Discarding the fork then leaves `undefined` instead of the old value, and a missing key is left behind as an own property holding `undefined`:

```svelte
<script>
	import { fork } from 'svelte';

	const object = $state({ x: 1 });
	'x' in object;
</script>

<button
	onclick={() => {
		fork(() => {
			object.x = 2;
		}).discard();

		console.log(object.x); // 1 before #18944, undefined on main
	}}
>
	discard
</button>
```

## Summary

Fixes #37790.

### The problem

With `enableCustomTypeDefinitionForReanimated` (enabled automatically when react-native-reanimated is installed), the compiler types Reanimated's `useFrameCallback` with `noAlias: true`, like its other frozen hooks. It then treats the callback as non-escaping and drops its memoization scope, and the user's `useCallback` with it. The callback is a new function on every render.

`useFrameCallback` registers the callback in an effect keyed on its identity: `[callback, autostart]` in react-native-reanimated 4.5.3, `src/hook/useFrameCallback.ts`. So each render unregisters and re-registers it, and `timeSinceFirstFrame` restarts. Time-driven animations jump back to the start on every re-render.

### The change

This types `useFrameCallback` with `noAlias: false`, in both `Globals.ts` and the Rust port (`globals.rs`).

The other Reanimated hooks typed with `noAlias: true` that take worklets (`useAnimatedStyle`, `useAnimatedProps`, `useAnimatedScrollHandler`, `useAnimatedReaction`, `useDerivedValue`) build their dependencies from the worklet's `__closure` and `__workletHash`, not its identity. I checked this in 4.5.3. They keep `noAlias: true`, and their output is unchanged: `reanimated-no-memo-arg` still passes as-is.

### Before and after

The reporter's pattern:

```js
function useGlowClock(time) {
  const onFrame = useCallback(
    frameInfo => {
      time.set(frameInfo.timeSinceFirstFrame);
    },
    [time]
  );
  useFrameCallback(onFrame);
}
```

- **Before:** `const onFrame = (frameInfo) => {...}; useFrameCallback(onFrame);`, a new function on every render.
- **After:** `onFrame` is memoized on `time`, the same as when the callback is passed to any other hook.

## How did you test this change?

- **New fixture, `reanimated-use-frame-callback-memoized`.**
  - Without the fix, its compiled output has no memo cache. With the fix, it is memoized on `time`.
  - It fails on the Rust backend when only the TypeScript side of the fix is applied, and passes with both sides.
- **End to end.**
  - I compiled the hook above with the plugin and rendered it in React.
  - A stand-in `useFrameCallback` registered the callback in an effect keyed on `[callback, autostart]`, the same way Reanimated 4.5.3 does.
  - Over 6 renders with an unrelated state change, the frame callback was registered:

    | Build | Registrations |
    |---|---|
    | No compiler | 1 |
    | Compiler, before this change | 6 |
    | Compiler, after this change | 1 |

  - The results were the same with and without a `'worklet'` directive.
- **Fixture suites.**

### Motivation / Background

SQLite rolls back the transaction itself when a statement or `COMMIT` fails with errors such as `SQLITE_FULL`, `SQLITE_IOERR` or `SQLITE_NOMEM`. The SQLite3 adapter then still runs `ROLLBACK`, which fails with `cannot rollback - no transaction is active`. That second exception:

- replaces the original error. The caller gets `StatementInvalid: cannot rollback - no transaction is active`, and the real `SQLite3::FullException` is two levels down in `#cause`, so `rescue` and retry logic keyed on the real error never matches;
- escapes before `rollback_records` runs. Records created in the transaction stay `persisted?` and keep their `id` for rows that do not exist, and `after_rollback` callbacks do not fire.

Reproduced on `main` with stock SQLite (3.53.2, sqlite3 2.9.6). `PRAGMA max_page_count` makes the transaction run out of pages:

```ruby
Item.transaction do
  first = Item.create!(body: "x")
  50.times { Item.create!(body: "y" * 20_000) }
end
```

```
# before
ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid: SQLite3::SQLException: cannot rollback - no transaction is active
  <- ... <- SQLite3::FullException: database or disk is full
first.persisted? # => true, first.id # => 1, rows in table: 0, after_rollback calls: 0

# after
ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid: SQLite3::FullException: database or disk is full
first.persisted? # => false, first.id # => nil, after_rollback calls: 1
```

A real full disk does the same thing: a database on a 2 MB tmpfs whose `COMMIT` hits `SQLITE_FULL` gives the same output.

### Detail

`SQLite3Adapter#exec_rollback_db_transaction` now returns early when the raw connection reports no open transaction (`SQLite3::Database#transaction_active?`, which is `!sqlite3_get_autocommit`). The rest of the rollback path, including `rollback_records`, runs as before.

### Additional information

- Added `SQLite3AutoRollbackTest`. It fails without the change (`Expected #<SQLite3::SQLException: cannot rollback - no transaction is active> to be an instance of SQLite3::FullException`) and passes with it.
- `rake test:sqlite3` with the change: 9,890 runs, 0 failures. There is 1 error, `ConnectionHandlersMultiDbTest#test_switching_connections_with_database_url`, because `pg` isn't installed on my machine. It errors the same way without the change.

Closes #6102

## Problem

`HTTPDigestAuth` corrupts the `Authorization` header when credentials are passed as `bytes` (which older advice, e.g. in #5089, recommended for non-latin credentials):

```python
HTTPDigestAuth("Ondřej".encode("utf-8"), "heslíčko".encode("utf-8"))
# -> Digest username="b'Ond\xc5\x99ej'", ...
```

The bytes are interpolated into the header via an f-string, so their `repr` is rendered and the wrong value is hashed.

## Fix

Decode `bytes` username/password as UTF-8 at the top of `build_digest_header` before they are used in the header and the digest. `str` credentials keep working exactly as before; `bytes` now produce the correct `username="Ondřej"` and matching digest.

## Tests

Added `test_DIGEST_AUTH_ACCEPTS_BYTES_CREDENTIALS` (no network) asserting both `str` and `bytes` credentials render `username="Ondřej"`. Full digest suite passes (7 passed). Added a HISTORY.md entry.

## Summary

Refs #37560.

`parseTypedArray` in `ReactFlightReplyServer` looks up the backing entry for a typed array or `ArrayBuffer` reference (`$A`, `$O`, `$o`, `$U`, `$S`, …) and calls `.arrayBuffer()` on it without checking its type. If a reply body points that reference at a plain string field, or at an entry that doesn't exist, decoding fails with an opaque `TypeError`:

- string entry: `backingEntry.arrayBuffer is not a function`
- missing entry: `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'arrayBuffer')`

The `$B` (Blob) case already guards this with `instanceof Blob` (#36055). This PR adds the same guard to `parseTypedArray`, so both paths reject with `Referenced Blob is not a Blob.` The message reuses the existing error code, so no new code is needed.

The issue's open question (whether a reference may come before its values) is left alone. A typed array reference always needs its bytes, so a missing or non-Blob entry is invalid either way.

## How did you test this change?

I added two tests to `ReactFlightDOMReply-test.js`, mirroring the existing `$B` test: one where a `$U` reference points at a string field and one where its entry is missing. Both fail on `main` with the TypeErrors above and pass with this change.

text:
### Motivation / Background

Refs #59028.

Since #58306 gave `HashConfig` value equality, `establish_connection` reuses
the existing connection pool for an equal configuration even when that
configuration was newly built. In Rails 8.1.4, an existing pool was reused
only when `establish_connection` resolved to the exact configuration object
that pool was established with, so passing a configuration hash, or an
environment name after rebuilding `configurations`, always established a new
pool. Code that relied on that, such as test setups that expect a fresh
SQLite `:memory:` database on each `establish_connection`, now gets the old
database back.

`ConnectionHandler#establish_connection` already accepts `clobber:` to skip
reuse, but `ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection` doesn't expose it, so
the only public way to force a new pool is to call `remove_connection` first.

### Detail

This Pull Request adds `clobber:` to `ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection`
and passes it through to the handler:

```ruby
ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(
  { adapter: "sqlite3", database: ":memory:" },
  clobber: true
)
```

The default stays `clobber: false`, so main's pool-reuse behavior is
unchanged; the keyword lets callers be explicit about which behavior they
want.

To keep brace-less calls such as
`establish_connection(adapter: "sqlite3", database: ":memory:")` working, the
signature is `establish_connection(config_or_env = nil, clobber: false,
**config)`: remaining keywords are treated as the configuration, and passing
a configuration both positionally and as keywords raises `ArgumentError`.

### Additional information

#59028 also asks whether the new reuse is intended for configuration hashes.
If restoring the 8.1 behavior is preferred instead, this keyword is still
useful for being explicit, but I'm happy to rework or close this.

When rewriteFixedLoad folds a pointer load out of a read-only symbol,
it marks the loaded symbol as used in an interface if its name has the
"type:" prefix. That prefix also matches helper symbols such as
type:.eqfunc.*, which is what the Equal field of a type descriptor
points to. After inlining reflect.TypeFor[T]().Comparable() on a struct
needing a generated equality function, the load of Equal is folded and
the function gets an R_USEIFACE relocation against type:.eqfunc.*,
making the linker panic because the target is not a type or itab.

Add (*LSym).IsGoType, which reports whether a symbol is a type
descriptor by name: a "type:" symbol whose name does not continue with
".". Use it both in rewriteFixedLoad and in the object writer's
SymFlagGoType check, so the two cannot disagree.

Fixes #81990

Linux time64 syscalls use `__kernel_timespec`, with signed 64-bit seconds and nanoseconds. The MIPS runtime currently uses an `int32` nanoseconds field followed by padding. On big-endian MIPS this puts nanoseconds in the upper half of the syscall field, causing subsecond futex waits and profiling intervals to be interpreted as zero.

Use two `int64` fields for the time64 representation, and explicitly narrow nanoseconds when converting to the legacy time32 representation. Add deterministic tests for the syscall representation and legacy conversion, including fractional seconds and boundary values.

Fixes #82147.

Validation against upstream master:

- New ABI test fails before the fix on Linux/mips hardware: `setNsec(1)` encodes `[0 4294967296]` instead of `[0 1]`. Both new tests pass after the fix.
- Both new tests pass under QEMU user emulation for Linux/mipsle, Linux/386 and Linux/arm; the ABI test passes on native Linux/amd64.
- Existing `runtime/pprof` tests `TestCPUProfile` and `TestCPUProfileMultithreaded` pass on Linux/mips hardware and collect samples.
- Upstream toolchain bootstrap, affected test-binary builds, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. The full test suite was not run.

The tests check the kernel syscall ABI rather than the kernel-internal `timespec64`, which has a different nanoseconds type on 32-bit systems. Legacy conversion tests cover the runtime fallback representation; execution on a kernel without time64 support remains unverified.

Implemented and verified with GPT-6.1-sol through the Codex harness.

Fixes #4965.

Previously, if reading `response.content` raised an exception (e.g. `ChunkedEncodingError` from an incomplete chunked response), the exception propagated on the first access, but `_content` stayed at its initial sentinel value (`False`) and `_content_consumed` stayed `False`. A second access to `.content` would then attempt to re-read the underlying stream. Since the connection is often already dead after the first failure, this second attempt silently "succeeded" with no data, so `.content` returned `b''` instead of raising -- masking the original error entirely, as described in the issue.

**Fix**: add a `_content_error` attribute that stores the exception raised while reading content. If set, `.content` re-raises it on every subsequent access instead of attempting (and silently succeeding at) reading an already-broken stream again.

**Verification**: added a regression test using a stateful fake `raw` object that faithfully reproduces the real urllib3 behavior being worked around -- raises once on the first `.stream()` call, then yields no further data (no error) on a second call, simulating a dead connection. I confirmed the test fails without the fix (second access returns `b''` instead of raising) and passes with it.

Ran the existing non-network-dependent test suite; results are identical to a clean checkout of `main` aside from the one new passing test (pre-existing `httpbin` fixture and network-dependent failures/errors in this sandbox are present on a clean `main` checkout too, unrelated to this change).

When a callback reads both `foo?.bar` and a guarded `foo.bar`, `exhaustive-deps` can suggest `[foo.bar]`. ## Summary

Fixes #37695.

`listenToAllSupportedEvents` used one marker property (`_reactListening…`) for two separate things:

1. "This root container already has its delegated listeners."
2. "This document already has the `selectionchange` listener."

With a normal element root, the container and its document are different objects, so sharing the marker is harmless. When the root container is the document itself (`createRoot(document)` / `hydrateRoot(document, …)`, which is how Next.js App Router mounts), the two collide:

- **The document is the root:** the root marks the document, then the `selectionchange` check sees the marker and skips attaching. `onSelect` never fires for selection changes that only arrive via `selectionchange` (`setSelectionRange()` from code, dragging selection handles on touch devices).
- **Another root is created first:** that root marks its owner document while attaching `selectionchange`. A later `createRoot(document)` sees the marker and returns early, attaching none of its event listeners.

This PR gives the document-level `selectionchange` listener its own marker, so the two checks are independent. Deduplication of each listener is unchanged.

## How did you test this change?

Added two regression tests to `ReactDOMEventListener-test.js`:

- `should subscribe to selectionchange when the root container is the document`
- `should listen to events on a document root created after another root`

Both fail on `main` (`Expected number of calls: 1, Received: 0`) and pass with this change.

The second test uses `keydown` rather than `click`: with `enableLegacyFBSupport` (www), clicks are deferred to a one-time listener added to the document during dispatch, which doesn't fire when the root container is the document itself. That's existing behavior separate from this bug.

Commands run:

yarn prettier
yarn linc
yarn flow dom-node                     # No errors!
yarn test     'ReactDOMEventListener|SelectEventPlugin|ReactDOMRoot|ReactDOMSingletonComponents|DOMPluginEventSystem'   # pass
yarn test-www 'ReactDOMEventListener|SelectEventPlugin|ReactDOMRoot|ReactDOMSingletonComponents|DOMPluginEventSystem'   # pass

text:
[DevTools] Don't remount the extension on same-document navigations (#37780)

## Summary

Fixes #37681.

Since Chrome 153, `chrome.devtools.network.onNavigated` also fires for
same-document navigations. [devtools-frontend CL
8155971](https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/devtools/devtools-frontend/+/8155971)
made `Page.navigatedWithinDocument` call `setInspectedURL()`, and the
DevTools extension server forwards every inspected URL change to
extensions as `onNavigated`. The callback only gets the URL. In Chrome
154 it fires for `pushState`, `replaceState` (including same-URL and
state-only calls), hash changes, intercepted Navigation API navigations
and `history.back()` within the document.

The extension treated every event as a new page. It unmounted the
panels, sent `shutdown` to the backend that was still running in the
page, and remounted. So every client-side route change lost the
selection and any in-progress Profiler recording. The remount itself was
also unreliable. The content script only says hello to the backend
manager once per document, so the re-injected backend manager depended
on timing. In some runs the page had no backend until the Components
panel was opened. In others, the new backend sent its initial tree
before the new frontend was listening.

Changes:

- **`main/index.js`, `evalScripts.js`:** only remount when the inspected
document was replaced. Keep the current instance if both of these hold:
  - it already received `extensionBackendInitialized`;
- the page still has `__REACT_DEVTOOLS_BACKEND_MANAGER_INJECTED__`. The
backend manager removes that flag when it shuts down, including on
`pagehide`, so bfcache restores still remount, and a new document never
has it.

If the check fails, it falls back to the old behavior. No new
permissions.
- **`backendManager.js`, `proxy.js`:** when the backend manager is
injected into a document whose previous backend shut down, it asks the
content script to say hello again. It now only accepts a hello as the
welcome message. Before, any message forwarded from the frontend
counted, including the old instance's `shutdown`, which could initialize
the backend while no frontend was listening.
- **`elementSelection.js`, `main/index.js`:** the remount now happens
one eval round trip later, which exposed a race. The Elements panel
selection sync could call `bridge.send` after that Bridge was shut down,
throwing "Cannot send a message through a Bridge that has been shut
down." It now only sends through the current instance's Bridge.

#37708 takes a different approach: it switches Chromium to
`webNavigation.onCommitted` and adds the `webNavigation` permission.

Firefox doesn't emit `onNavigated` for same-document navigations, so
nothing should change there, but I didn't test Firefox.

## How did you test this change?

- `yarn prettier`, `yarn linc`: pass.
- `yarn flow dom-browser`, which covers `react-devtools-extensions`, and
`yarn flow dom-node`: no errors.
- `yarn test-build-devtools --silent --no-watchman
react-devtools-extensions`: 2/2 pass. `ignoreList-test.js` builds the
extension in development and production modes. The source and www Jest
configs exclude the DevTools packages, so `yarn test` and `yarn
test-www` match no tests.
- `yarn build-for-devtools && yarn build:chrome:local`: the extension
built from this branch loads in Chrome 154.

End to end, I drove the real DevTools UI in headless Chrome
154.0.8037.93 over CDP, with an isolated profile and a React 18 SPA test
page. The Components and Profiler panels were opened with
`InspectorFrontendAPI.showPanel`. The checks were the backend agent's
identity in the page, the bridge traffic, and the rendered Components
tree. Shipped 8.0.0 compared with this branch:

| Scenario | 8.0.0 | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Router `pushState` ×2, state-only `replaceState`, hash change,
`history.back()` within the document | Remounts on every navigation:
`shutdown` sent, new backend agent each time | Same backend agent; the
tree follows the route |
| Components panel hidden while navigating | No backend in the page
until the panel is opened | Backend stays connected |
| Profiling across two route changes | Recording lost ("No profiling
data has been recorded") | 4 commits recorded |
| Reload, link to another document, bfcache restore, cross-site
navigation | Remounts | Remounts; the tree shows the new document |

The backend-manager change on its own, with the shipped `main.js`, also
fixes the remount itself: after a same-document remount, the new backend
attaches immediately instead of waiting for the Components panel to be
opened (2/2 runs).

Closing and reopening DevTools without a reload shows an empty tree in
8.0.0 too. That's a separate issue; I closed DevTools over CDP, which
may not match a user closing it. On this branch, the next navigation
remounts and recovers it, as before.

Fixes #37785.

## Summary

`areHookInputsEqual` loops only up to `min(prevDeps.length, nextDeps.length)`. When a hook's deps array grows or shrinks between renders, the extra entries are never compared, so the hook treats the inputs as unchanged:

- `useMemo` / `useCallback` return a stale value.
- `useEffect` / `useLayoutEffect` skip a re-run that should happen.

This PR returns `false` when the two arrays differ in length, in both the reconciler (`ReactFiberHooks.js`) and the Fizz server renderer (`ReactFizzHooks.js`). The dev-only "changed size between renders" warning is unchanged.

`res.json()` sets `Content-Type` to `application/json; charset=utf-8`, and then `res.send()` runs `setCharset` on it, which parses and re-formats the same string with `content-type`. `res.send(string)` hits the same path after `res.type('html')`.

This adds an early return in `setCharset` when the value is already a lowercase `type/subtype; charset=utf-8` with no other params. Everything else (other charsets, uppercase, extra params) still goes through the parser, so the output is unchanged.

A micro benchmark of `setCharset('application/json; charset=utf-8', 'utf-8')` goes from ~350ns to ~30ns per call on Node 24. I only measured the helper, not a full request.

Added tests for case normalization and extra params.

## Description

When a client disconnects mid-stream, the WSGI server abandons the body
iterator. The generator is later finalized by the garbage collector, often
on a **different thread** than the one that pushed the context.

`ctx.pop()` raises `RuntimeError` because `_cv_app.get(None)` returns `None`
on the GC thread. The context stays "stuck" on the original worker thread,
and `teardown_appcontext` never fires for subsequent requests on that thread.

## Fix

Replace `with ctx:` with manual `ctx.push()` / `ctx.pop()` in the
`stream_with_context` generator. Wrap `pop()` in a try/except that catches
`RuntimeError` and resets the context state (`_push_count` and `_cv_token`)
to prevent thread pool poisoning.

## Related

- #5774 fixed the same cross-context token failure for async views
- #5804 covers teardown ordering in the 3.1.2 rewrite

Closes #6123
